# Workflows

| Workflow | Runs on | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`ci.yml`](ci.yml) | Push to `main` and pull requests | On Linux, macOS and Windows it checks formatting, runs Clippy with warnings as errors, runs the tests and plays every game without a terminal at three sizes. On Linux it also runs `scripts/snapshots.sh` and fails when the stills in `docs/images` or the showcase frames in `docs/frames` differ from what the program draws. It builds the Intel macOS target and the static x86-64 and ARM64 Linux targets, since Lua is compiled from source with each target's C compiler. A last job checks the crate on Rust 1.88, the `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml` |
| [`release.yml`](release.yml) | A tag starting with `v`, such as `v0.1.0` | Builds every binary in the workspace for Apple silicon and Intel Macs, static Linux for x86-64 and ARM64 (musl) and 64 bit Windows with the C runtime linked statically (set in `.cargo/config.toml`). Each archive holds the games with the README, licence, notice, changelog, accessibility statement and guides plus a SHA-256 file. The files are attached to the GitHub release of that tag. The release is made by a maintainer from a signed tag, so the workflow waits up to twenty minutes for it to exist and never creates one itself. Rerunning it replaces the files. Attaching files to a published release needs immutable releases to stay off for this repository. Once every platform's files are attached, a last job sends a `games-release` repository dispatch naming the tag to `zacesshq/website`, so zacess.com rebuilds straight away. It reads the `SITE_DISPATCH_TOKEN` organisation secret, skips with a note in the run summary when that is not set and only reports a failed dispatch, never failing the release |
| [`markdownlint.yml`](markdownlint.yml) | Push to `main` and pull requests, also run by hand | Lints every markdown file with the rules in `.markdownlint.json` |

Every action is pinned to a full commit SHA with its version in a comment. Dependabot proposes updates
weekly for the actions and the Cargo dependencies.
